question.text:
A system has two processes, $P_1$ and $P_2$.

  • $P_1$ is currently running.
     
  • $P_2$ is ready.
     
  • The operating system uses preemptive Round Robin scheduling.
     
  • $P_1$'s scheduling quantum is about to expire.
     
  • $P_2$ will be selected to run next.
     

Consider the following events:

  1. $P_1$'s user-level state is saved into a trap frame.
     
  2. $P_2$'s user-level state is saved into a trap frame.
     
  3. A timer interrupt occurs.
     
  4. The operating system scheduler runs.
     
  5. A context switch occurs from the thread of $P_1$ to the thread of $P_2$.
     
  6. $P_1$'s user-level state is restored.
     
  7. $P_2$'s user-level state is restored.
     
  8. A system-call instruction is executed.
     
  9. The thread of $P_2$ is created.
     
  10. The thread of $P_1$ is destroyed.
     

Which sequence correctly describes the events?

  1. $3,1,4,5,7$
     
  2. $3,4,1,7,5$
     
  3. $1,3,5,4,7$
     
  4. $3,1,5,4,6$

Assume:

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true about a scheduler that implements a Round Robin scheduling policy?

  1. This scheduler will minimize the number of context switches when scheduling processes that never sleep or wait for I/O.
     
  2. This scheduler has higher throughput than a First-Come First-Served policy.
     
  3. This scheduler will approximately evenly divide CPU time between processes that never sleep or wait for I/O.
     
  4. It is possible to implement a Round Robin scheduler such that selecting the next process to run and marking a process as runnable takes $O(1)$ time.
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Consider the following workload:

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{Job} & \text{Arrival Time} & \text{CPU Burst Time} \\ \hline A & 0 & 8 \\ B & 2 & 4 \\ C & 5 & 7 \end{array}$$

Assume Round Robin scheduling with a time slice of $1$ second.

What is the turnaround time of job $B$?

  1. $8$ seconds
     
  2. $9$ seconds
     
  3. $10$ seconds
     
  4. $11$ seconds

question.text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

  1. A Round Robin scheduler may preempt the currently running job.
     
  2. A Shortest-Time-to-Completion-First scheduler cannot cause jobs to starve.
     
  3. If all jobs arrive at the same point in time, SJF and Shortest-Time-to-Completion-First will behave the same.
     
  4. If all jobs have identical run lengths, Round Robin provides worse average turnaround time than FIFO.
